title: Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents
claim: A closed-loop search that retrieves, proposes, evaluates and stores candidates accumulates knowledge, matching baseline accuracy at lower cost and transferring.
layout: Top 4-stage loop under a library bar; bottom 3 result panels, left-to-right
description: The figure has two halves. The top half is a method pipeline. A wide rounded bar labeled 'Strategy Library' with a database icon spans the top, under a 'Code' heading with a GitHub logo. Below it are four pastel boxes joined by arrows: 1 Retrieve (green), 2 Propose (blue), 3 Evaluate (orange) and 4 Accumulate (purple). A 'read' arrow runs from the library into box 1. A 'write' arrow runs from box 4 back up to the library. A looping arrow underneath is labeled 'repeat and keep best'. The bottom half has three outlined panels. 'Full search' and 'One-shot retrieval' each show paired horizontal bars for accuracy and cost, comparing baseline (gray) with ours (green for accuracy, blue for cost) and giving cost reductions of 39% and 23%. 'Cross-model transfer' is a small table listing Qwen3, GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5 with accuracy gains and cost ratios. The eye goes first to the colorful pipeline.
caption: Strategist turns strategy design into a search that accumulates knowledge. Top: in each round, an LLM writes new inference strategies as code, runs them, and stores every one, with its measured accuracy and cost, in a library shared across tasks, so later tasks build on what earlier ones found. The models stay frozen; only the strategies change. Bottom: the search matches the strongest baseline (BL) at lower cost, and its strategies work on new tasks and new models without further search. Cost ratios are per-benchmark averages; transfer costs are totals in USD.
abstract: A model is only half of an AI agent system. The other half is the inference strategy: the reasoning procedure that turns model calls into a response. Today that second half is written by hand, and the experience of building one strategy never carries to the next. We introduce Strategist, a meta-agent that evolves inference strategies across tasks. Each strategy is written as a blueprint,executable code that other strategies can reuse, and together the blueprints form a library. Given a task and a small development set, Strategist retrieves related blueprints, writes candidate strategies, tests them on real samples, and revises them from the results. Every candidate then enters the library, so later tasks build on earlier discoveries. On 30 benchmarks, Strategist beats the strongest baseline on 24 and matches its average accuracy (74.7% vs.74.0%) at 39% lower inference cost. Its strategies also transfer to unseen tasks and other models without further search. The part of an AI system that is not improved on its own now does.
